processing_steps.atmosphere: high vacuum (pressure below 10^-6 bar) then high-purity argon (pressure below 1 bar)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials >99.8 wt% pure placed in water-cooled copper crucible; remelting repeated at least five times to promote uniform composition and reduce gas contamination (O 12-89 ppm, N ~18 ppm, H ~2 ppm).
Applied to as-cast steels; Fig. S1 shows oxygen segregation to grain boundaries does not occur.
Hot-rolling with a thickness reduction of 40 %, followed by water quenching.
The hot-rolled plates were subjected to cold rolling with an 80 % reduction; micro shear bands produced act as preferred nucleation sites for recrystallization.
The Zr-alloyed cold-rolled plates were annealed at 900 °C for 5 min, followed by water quenching; this is the pre-deformation terminal state in which the bimodal heterogeneous grain structure forms.

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase bimodal heterogeneous FCC grain structure comprising coarse grain (CG) zones and fine grain (FG) zones, with a high density of nanoscale ZrC carbide particles; FG zones carry a high dislocation density (high KAM).

defects.dislocation_density: low (low KAM value relative to FG zones)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: bimodal histogram with a mode near 5 μm

defects.dislocation_density: high (high KAM value, dense dislocations decorate fine FCC grains)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: bimodal histogram with a mode near 2.5-3 μm / ~1 μm

precipitates.distribution: high density of fine particles uniformly distributed in FG regions and inside FCC grain interiors

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: A high density of dislocations is decorated around the nanotwinned region, contributing to dislocation-nanotwin interaction that reduces the mean free paths of mobile dislocations (twinning-induced plasticity); twin boundaries decorated by multiple stacking faults.
Numerous ~30 nm ZrC particles distributed in FCC grain interior effectively inhibit dislocation movement (precipitation/Orowan strengthening).

interfaces.slip_behavior: At minor plastic deformation planar slip (dislocations) is initially activated in the FCC matrix; after severe deformation a high density of slip bands forms along {111} planes, and nanotwins (~20 nm in size) form during heavy deformation.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Partial recrystallization during 900 °C/5 min annealing; Zr solute drag and Zener pinning of ZrC retard recrystallization, producing the bimodal FCC (CG+FG) heterogeneous grain structure.
interfaces.interface_notes: At 2 % global strain the CG zones and FG/CG hetero-interfaces experience high local strain while FG zones remain nearly undeformed (strain partitioning); at 8 % global strain FG zones also accumulate strain. Hardness difference between soft CG and hard FG zones drives geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) generation and HDI strengthening.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat dog-bone-shaped sample, gauge length 14 mm and width 4 mm, prepared along the rolling direction (RD)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Uniaxial tensile testing using Instron 5892 with a contact extensometer.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of Zr0.50 (Fig. 4a), plus true stress-strain curve in the inset (true stress up to ~1200 MPa, true strain 0-0.5).

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Zr0.50 (YS ~505 MPa, UTS ~855 MPa, fracture ductility 58 %) vs Zr0 (YS ~435 MPa, UTS 820 MPa, ductility 52 %) and vs Zr0.01 (YS ~450 MPa, UTS ~832 MPa, ductility 55 %); the Zr0.50 steel shows the best strength-ductility synergy and the largest, deepest and densest ductile dimples.

characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal the microstructure of the Zr0.50 steel showing CG and FG zones and fine FCC particles.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Zr0.50 steel exhibits a typical heterogeneous banded structure of coarse FCC grains (CG) and fine FCC grains (FG); a high density of fine FCC particles is uniformly distributed in the FG regions.

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD): IPF, IQ and KAM maps
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM equipped with an EBSD detector (accelerating voltage 30 kV, step size 500 nm)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Prior to deformation; KAM color bar 0-5
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal grain structure, grain size and local misorientation (dislocation density) of the Zr0.50 steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Zr0.50 exhibits a distinct heterostructure of CG and FG zones; FG zones exhibit high KAM values (high dislocation density) while CG zones show low KAM; grain orientations are random; fraction of CGs adjacent to FGs ~37 %.

characterization_methods.technique: Quasi-in-situ tensile testing with EBSD and μ-DIC (von Mises local strain mapping)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 5892 universal testing machine; SEM Hitachi SU7000; VIC-2D software; monolayer of nanoscale SiO2 particles as speckle pattern
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal local strain evolution/partitioning between FG and CG zones in the Zr0.50 steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Significant strain partitioning at 2 % global strain: CG zones and FG/CG hetero-interfaces experience high strain while FG zones remain nearly undeformed; at 8 % global strain the FG zones accumulate more strain, indicating persistent partitioning that generates GNDs and HDI strengthening.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: After tensile fracture; 10 µm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the fracture morphology of the Zr0.50 tensile specimen.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Zr0.50 fracture surface shows the largest, deepest and densest dimples with tearing ridges, consistent with high ductility.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL F200 operated at 200 kV; TEM foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in 5 % perchloric acid + 95 % ethanol (vol%).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: During/after tensile deformation (minor to severe deformation)
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal deformation mechanisms (dislocations, slip bands, nanotwins) and identify ZrC particles in the Zr0.50 steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dislocations activated first; slip bands along {111} after severe deformation; nanotwins ~20 nm with twin boundaries decorated by stacking faults; ~30 nm ZrC carbides confirmed by HRTEM/FFT (indexed <110>ZrC) distributed in FCC grain interior.

characterization_methods.purpose: Calculate equilibrium phase fractions of the Zr0.50 steel, particularly the ZrC fraction.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Above ~700 °C the matrix is single-phase FCC with a small, temperature-insensitive ZrC fraction (~0.6 % after annealing at 900 °C); BCC and κ carbide present only below ~700 °C.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated ZrC fraction ~0.6 % at 900 °C is consistent with the TEM-observed nanoscale ZrC precipitates in the annealed Zr0.50 steel.
Model predictions compared with the measured Zr0.50 yield strength (~505 MPa) and with EBSD grain-size/zone data.

analytical_models.equation_role: Describes the yield-strength contribution from FG and CG zones including back-stress-strengthened CGs adjacent to FGs

parameters.name: f_CG,b (fraction of CGs adjacent to FGs)

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimation of sigma_CG and sigma_FG used in Eq. 2

analytical_models.model_name: Back-stress strengthening of CG adjacent to FG (Eq. 4)
analytical_models.equation_role: Expresses sigma_CG,b, the back-stress strengthened CGs adjacent to FGs
Calculates strengthening from nanoscale ZrC carbides
Describes strain hardening in terms of SSD and GND densities and its decomposition into dislocation and HDI hardening
analytical_models.model_note: Increased GND density in the heterostructured Zr0.50 steel gives extra HDI hardening and HDI ductility.

analytical_models.equation_role: Estimates the critical stress for deformation twinning in FCC alloys
analytical_models.model_note: Critical twinning stress ~1.14 GPa is lower than the true ultimate tensile strength of Zr0.50, enabling deformation twinning.

unmapped_findings: The Zr0.50 steel exhibits a true ultimate tensile strength (Fig. 4a inset) that exceeds its critical twinning stress of ~1.14 GPa; the exact true UTS value is not reported numerically.
Strengthening budget of the Zr0.50 steel: grain-boundary strengthening + HDI strengthening ~300 MPa and ZrC precipitation (Orowan) strengthening 108 MPa.
Stacking fault energy (SFE) of the FCC matrix in the Zr0.50 steel is estimated to be ~55 mJ/m^2 (Supplementary text S1).
Deformation nanotwins in the Zr0.50 steel are ~20 nm in size, with twin boundaries decorated by multiple stacking faults, indicating formation from multiple Shockley partial dislocations.
ZrC precipitates in the Zr0.50 steel are ~30 nm in size with a fraction of 0.006 (~0.6 %) after 900 °C annealing, consistent with the Thermo-Calc calculation.
The {111} slip bands and nanotwinning in the deformed Zr0.50 steel provide additional strengthening and enable twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP).
